symptom: Every GUID in a ChangeDataCapture$EntityChangeDataCaptureService read back as the empty string: EntityGuid on each baseline source, PropertyGuid and AssociatedEntityGuid on each baseline property. The rest of the document decoded fine — exposed names, Type enums, the live sources, the entity references — so the failure was invisible except by printing the GUIDs. Measured on ako/TestApp 619864b (Mendix 11.16.1): 8 of 8 GUID fields empty.
cause: The vendored gen typed EntityGuid/PropertyGuid as property.Primitive[string] with property.DecodeString, but Mendix stores every GUID as BSON binary subtype 0. DecodeString does `s, _ := val.StringValueOK()` and DISCARDS the ok flag, so a binary value yields "" with no error. Four further properties Studio Pro writes were absent from the gen entirely (AppName, VersionedSourcePointer, VersionedPropertyPointer, AssociatedEntityGuid) because they are not in the vendored reflection data.
file: modelsdk/gen/changedatacapture/types.go (hand-edited: the generator is not in-tree); guard tests in modelsdk/gen/changedatacapture/handadded_test.go
fix: Type every binary GUID as property.ByIdRef[element.Element] and decode it the way domainmodels decodes ParentPointer — StringValueOK first, then BinaryOK + codec.BinaryToUUID. ByIdRef also encodes correctly: the codec turns a non-empty element.ID into binary via idToBinary. Accessors keep their string signatures (EntityGuid() string) so no caller changes. The four missing properties are added to the struct, the accessors, init (sequential Bind index + SetProperties) and InitFromRaw.
test: modelsdk/gen/changedatacapture/handadded_test.go: binary decode per GUID field, the live->baseline pointers, AppName, and a round-trip pinning codec.BinaryToUUID against mpr.IDToBsonBinary on the fixture's real GUIDs. Control: restoring DecodeString makes each fail with `= ""`, which is the reported symptom.
insight: A decode helper that drops its ok flag turns a type mismatch into a plausible empty value, and an empty GUID is indistinguishable from an unset one — nothing downstream can tell. Grep gen for Primitive[string] on any property whose name ends in Guid before trusting a read. The subject matters as much as the field: only a Studio Pro-authored document has GUIDs that differ from $ID, so an mxcli-created one would have shown nothing wrong. And the proposal that mapped this document listed FOUR missing properties from the HAM schema; the fifth defect was in a property that was present, which is why a schema diff alone was not enough — the values had to be printed.
